synthesis.description: Traders or desk heads ask for new EnronOnline products (a Super Peak 5x8 product, hourly products for hours ending 12-20), and operations and EOL staff define the product wording, availability hours, the index each product maps to, and the books traders log in with. Draft product content is circulated for approval or comment, schedulers are briefed on how the new products are ticketed, and product lists are assigned to traders and later revisited in a second pass.
steps: A desk requests a new EOL product and a target launch, such as by bid week.
EOL staff draft the product description, hours and terms.
Operations is asked to approve or comment on the product wording.
The index for the product is mapped to the EOL indexes and books are set for trader log-in.
Products are assigned to traders and the list is reviewed again.
Schedulers and Sitara users are briefed on how the new deals flow and are ticketed.
synthesis.approach: Use a standard product request form that captures product wording, delivery hours, index mapping, book and trader assignment and the approver before set-up starts, and route it through a fixed approval sequence that notifies schedulers and Sitara users on launch.
synthesis.rationale: Delays and rework come from details that surface late (index mapping, books, trader lists, ticketing comments); a request template gathers them up front, while product design and approval remain judgement calls.
